native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: Diversity in Pottery Form collapsed while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased simultaneously in the 18th century BCE (BCE 1800-1701; first registered at 1700 BCE / CE -1700): PotteryForm Z 0.74 -> -1.13 (delta -1.87, largest single-century drop in record) and PotteryDecoration Z -0.48 -> 0.97 (delta +1.45) in the same 100-year window; the only such simultaneous century, with a persistent post-event plateau (Form -1.13 through 500 BCE; Decoration 0.97 then 1.53).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected 3 datasets: time_series_data.csv (annual CE -4100..-500; PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration sparse centennial raw + fully interpolated _inter), capital.csv (BCE 4300..500 centennial grid; ZKeform=PotteryForm, Zkeverz=PotteryDecoration, German decimal commas; period groups EN/MN/SG/LN/OBA/YBA), pollen file (auxiliary, no pottery data; calBP/CE offset inconsistent). 2) Cross-validated capital.csv vs time_series_data.csv pottery indices: max abs diff = 0.0 over 37 matched centuries -> identical, used capital.csv BCE grid as canonical. 3) Computed per-century changes (oldest->newest): identified the unique strict same-century step BCE 1800->1700 with dForm=-1.87 and dDec=+1.45. 4) Sensitivity checks: magnitude thresholds (|dForm|>0.5..1.5, dDec>=0.5..1.0 all give the same single step; threshold 2.0 removes all), +-1-century overlap (band of centers 1400..2000 BCE all capture the same event), and corroboration via annual interpolated series (only 100-y window 1800->1700 has Form collapse + Decoration rise). 5) Persistence: collapsed Form (-1.13) and elevated Decoration (0.97 -> 1.53) sustained for all subsequent centuries. Final: 18th century BCE (BCE 1800-1701), first new-state grid value 1700 BCE (CE -1700).

sub_hypo.text: Diversity in Pottery Form collapsed while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased during the 18th century BCE, first registered at 1700 BCE. This was the only simultaneous century with these changes, followed by persistent low Form and elevated Decoration values through 500 BCE.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological pottery indices on the canonical capital.csv centennial BCE grid (4300–500 BCE), cross-validated against time_series_data.csv over 37 matched centuries. The event occurred in the 1800–1700 BCE step, representing the 18th century BCE (1800–1701 BCE), with the new state first recorded at 1700 BCE (CE -1700); persistence extends through 500 BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: In the same 100-year window, PotteryForm (ZKeform) fell from 0.74 to -1.13 (delta -1.87), the largest single-century drop in the record, while PotteryDecoration (Zkeverz) rose from -0.48 to 0.97 (delta +1.45). This simultaneous collapse and rise occurred in only one century and was corroborated by the annual interpolated series. Form remained at -1.13 through 500 BCE, while Decoration remained elevated at 0.97 and subsequently 1.53.
